items.title: Requested payment for private register entry (offer, not a real debt)
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date for payment: 01.12.2026. No period calculation is needed since an explicit date is given. Note: the letter itself states 'Dieses Schreiben ist ein Angebot. Mit Ihrer Zahlung nehmen Sie es an; ein Vertrag kommt erst durch die Zahlung zustande.' This means no contract and no payment obligation exist unless the recipient chooses to pay. The date 2026-12-01 is therefore only the sender's requested deadline for accepting their offer, not an enforceable due date.

warnings: This document has the hallmarks of a known German scam pattern: a private company sends an invoice-styled letter for entry into a private, non-official 'Grundstücksregister' that has no connection to the official German Grundbuch (land registry), trying to make recipients believe they must pay for a legally required registration.

The letter itself admits (in small print) that it is only an 'Angebot' (offer) and that no contract exists until payment is made — i.e. there is no pre-existing debt or legal obligation to pay the 498,00 EUR; paying would be voluntarily entering into a contract for a service of essentially no value.

The sender explicitly states the entry 'steht in keinem Zusammenhang mit dem amtlichen Grundbuch' (has no connection to the official land registry), confirming this is a commercial private-register offer, not an official fee.

Recommendation: do not pay this invoice; it is not a legally binding demand. If in doubt, verify with the local Grundbuchamt or consumer protection agency (Verbraucherzentrale) before taking any action.
